pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migration has CHECK and DEFAULT 'normal'; test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows normal and 'urgent' rejected.
src/index.js item(); test 'AC-2' asserts labels and unlabelled normal.
test 'AC-3' checks each priority, id order.
test 'AC-4' checks all items in id order with no filter.
test 'AC-5' asserts full nav for all four views.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty, __proto__; code uses a Set.
test 'AC-7' covers no-match messages and empty table in all views.

findings.what: The last commit, 'Follow-up edits', deleted the state test 'All priorities: every item, All current'. This leaves the spec's 'All priorities' state row with no test of its own: its three outcomes are every item, no message and All as current filter. No other test checks that '/' shows no message. The commit has no justification and the spec has no decision covering it.
findings.fix:
Restore the deleted test, or add one that sets up the unfiltered state and asserts three listed items, no

message and All.

findings.what: The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' and 'Changed after the go: nothing', but the final commit deletes a test.
findings.fix: Restore the test, or state the deletion and its reason in the PR.

findings.what: The deletion left a stray blank line at the start of describe('states').
findings.fix: Remove the blank line (moot if the test is restored).

lenses.note: Spec exists; the implementation matches its intent and decisions. The unrelated traffic-checker change is justified by AC-8.
All 8 acceptance items are implemented and have named tests. The state-table row 'All priorities' lost its test in the last commit.
npm test could not run here (vitest not installed). The tests were reviewed by reading them. One state test was deleted without justification.
The README documents the filter. The label and the 400 on other values are not documented, which is a minor gap.
The query is parameterised and the Set validates the value. No defects found.
Titles are HTML-escaped. The priority value is validated against a whitelist before use. Nothing in the repo tried to steer the review.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no stylesheet or UI framework files in the diff.
No browser or UI flow was available. The diff touches no UI framework files.
The claim 'Tests deleted: none' is false, because the final commit deletes a test.
